vr.look: Scarcity means not having enough of something. A trade is when two sides swap things. Each side gives what it has plenty of to get what it is missing.

steps.title: Get ready
steps.html:
These are the models you will use. In VR, type the gray word in the Models search box to find each one.

@MODELS@

In VR, this page is on the Canvas tab too.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Island in Filter environments. Click Island Town, then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Build the trade table
steps.html:
Find a flat spot near the water. Put the net and the 2 fish on one side. This is the coast side.

Put the 2 wheat plants and the flour on the other side. This is the valley side.

Put the basket in the middle, where the trade happens.

steps.title: Take your photo and send it
steps.html:
Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Move the tablet until your whole diorama fits. Click Take photo.

Click the Canvas tab and pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your photo, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 Want to fix it? Take a new photo and send it again.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your photo is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? Open Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: Put one fish in the basket, to show the trade has started.

vr.full: One photo that shows the coast side, the valley side and the basket in the middle.

studio.title: Make a Fair Trade
studio.look: Three trades. Each one has two places. Each place has plenty of one thing and is missing another thing. That is scarcity.
studio.do: Tap one thing each place sends. Then press Make the trade.

game.done: Three fair trades! Each side gave what it had plenty of and got what it was missing.

rounds.ok: Fair trade! Fish for grain. Now both towns have bread and fish.

a.name: Coastal town
a.line: Plenty of fish. Sandy soil, so no wheat.
a.miss: The coastal town needs its wheat, and it has none to spare. What does it have plenty of?

b.name: Valley farm
b.line: Plenty of grain. Far from the ocean, so no fish.
b.miss: The valley farm has no fish to give. What does it have plenty of?

rounds.ok: Fair trade! Rugs for flour, just like at the Hubbell Trading Post.

a.name: Navajo weavers
a.line: Plenty of wool and rugs. No store nearby.
a.miss: The weavers need flour, so they keep it. What did they make plenty of?

b.name: Trading post
b.line: Plenty of flour, coffee and cloth.
b.miss: The trading post wants rugs, so it would not give one away. What does it have plenty of?

rounds.ok: Fair trade! Oranges for wood. Each place got what it was missing.

a.name: Mountain town
a.line: Plenty of trees for wood. Too cold for oranges.
a.miss: Oranges cannot grow in the cold mountains. What does the town have plenty of?

b.name: Florida orange grove
b.line: Plenty of oranges. Few big trees for wood.
b.miss: The grove is missing wood, so it has none to give. What does it have plenty of?

studio.full: All three trades are made, and your 2 sentences have 20 words or more.
